transcript.text: Good morning everyone. As you know, Line 6 is scheduled to produce 1,400 medical-device housings this week, but R-17 resin is temporarily unavailable. We have an alternate medical-grade resin, R-22, available for a controlled run. Before I issue the engineering authorization for this change, I need to hear from each of you on any constraints. Quality, process engineering, regulatory affairs, and production planning — please share any concerns or requirements you have so we can proceed properly through change-control. What do we need to address?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I checked the customer's revised control plan this morning. It specifies that an alternate-resin run requires dimensional and tensile testing on exactly 50 first-off housings, with all 50 passing before the run can be released, plus retention of exactly 10 samples. I also need to flag that the revised plan has not yet been attached to the change-control record, so we need to get that linked before authorization.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share my process trial findings for R-22. My trial showed that R-22 must be dried at 80 degrees Celsius for exactly 4 hours and requires a 45-minute screw purge before molding. I recorded this in my engineering notebook but have not yet entered it into the production setup sheet, so we need to make sure these parameters are captured before production begins.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to raise a regulatory constraint. I confirmed with the resin manufacturer that the medical-grade declaration for R-22 applies only to supplier lot L2407-18. Our regulatory procedure requires lot-specific traceability and customer notification before any housings made from that lot can be shipped. I also want to flag that the supplier confirmation is currently only in my email and has not yet been placed in the release file, so we need to get that documentation formally filed before we proceed.
